essence: It stops praying for things and starts praying for Him: the wish-tree outgrows prayer-grounds (1), yet the self stays unjoined to the highest (2) though declared identical with the Lord (3); melt into His sight (4); when the amazement (5), the face (6), the flood (7), the soon (8); bring on everything including contradiction (9); rays face to face (10); thieves tamed (11); mind drowned (12); set the mortal on fitting ground (13); no siddhi-drop (14); I ask only this (15); feet blooming in mind (16); I have a Lord, a father, a mother — no second: I roam fulfilled (17).

sections.SUMMARY: It stops praying for things and starts praying for Him: the wish-tree outgrows prayer-grounds (1), yet the self stays unjoined to the highest (2) though declared identical with the Lord (3); melt into His sight (4); when the amazement (5), the face (6), the flood (7), the soon (8); bring on everything including contradiction (9); rays face to face (10); thieves tamed (11); mind drowned (12); set the mortal on fitting ground (13); no siddhi-drop (14); I ask only this (15); feet blooming in mind (16); I have a Lord, a father, a mother — no second: I roam fulfilled (17).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of revelation (udyota); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at praying for Him, not things. The rasa is the tranquility of revealed meaning — stopping prayer for things, starting prayer for Him. Lakshmanjoo: illumination (udyota) — stops praying for things, starts praying for Him. The wish-tree outgrows prayer-grounds. The rasa is the tranquility of revealed meaning — praying for Him, not things.
